answer: One defence is stake-weighted reputation that decays without useful work. Each agent must lock a deposit and earn trust only through verified, valuable tasks over time — like a sonnet that must be composed line by line, not copied in bulk. A newcomer starts at the meadow edge, able to do small jobs but unable to vote or move large value until its record grows. Creating thousands of fake identities then means funding thousands of deposits and doing real work for each, pushing the attacker off the ledge of profitability: the cost of faking scale exceeds any reward the fakes could extract.
